scope: Australian political, electoral and parliamentary terminology used to understand the political domain. MAYHEM/site architecture and sport-legibility interface terms are excluded and belong in the separate Site Master Glossary.
rules: Preserve native political terminology as encountered in authoritative sources.
Do not place MAYHEM architecture, audit-state or sport-translation terminology in this glossary.
Use authoritative Australian electoral and parliamentary sources where available.
A glossary entry is a research aid, not evidence of a political proposition by itself.

terms.plain_language: More than half of the formal votes in a House of Representatives election.
terms.research_use: Determine whether a candidate has won without further preference distribution.

terms.plain_language: A method of secret voting, normally in written form.
terms.research_use: Anchor voting-process terminology.

terms.plain_language: An election held to fill a single vacancy in the House of Representatives.
terms.research_use: Identify seat-specific electoral contests outside a general election.

terms.plain_language: A person formally nominated to stand for election.
terms.research_use: Separate declared or endorsed contenders from formally nominated candidates.

terms.plain_language: An alliance between political parties formed for electoral, parliamentary or governing purposes.
terms.research_use: Track relationships between parties without collapsing them into one party object.

terms.plain_language: Members or senators who are neither part of the government nor the official opposition.
terms.research_use: Track balance-of-power actors and voting blocs.

terms.plain_language: The formal statement of an election result.
terms.research_use: Identify authoritative outcome finalisation.

terms.plain_language: The process used to determine the winning candidate when no candidate has an absolute majority of first-preference votes.
terms.research_use: Analyse how lower preferences affect final outcomes.

terms.plain_language: A formal recorded vote in a house of Parliament; the word is also used for a House of Representatives electorate in electoral administration.
terms.research_use: Disambiguate parliamentary voting from electoral geography.

terms.plain_language: The body of electors in an electoral area; commonly used for the electoral area itself.
terms.research_use: Anchor seat-level analysis and representation.

terms.plain_language: A parliament in which no political party or coalition holds a majority in the House of Representatives.
terms.research_use: Identify government-formation and balance-of-power conditions.

terms.plain_language: A candidate or parliamentarian who does not belong to a registered political party.
terms.research_use: Keep independent actors separate from synthetic party groupings.

terms.plain_language: A vote not marked according to the rules and therefore unable to be counted toward the result.
terms.research_use: Interpret turnout and vote totals correctly.

terms.plain_language: AEC terminology for a seat where the elected candidate received less than 56 per cent of the vote.
terms.research_use: Flag electorates with relatively narrow prior margins.

terms.plain_language: A member of the executive government responsible for a portfolio or area of administration.
terms.research_use: Track executive responsibility and portfolio changes.

terms.plain_language: A parliamentary motion or vote expressing dissatisfaction with a government or minister; a successful House no-confidence motion may lead to resignation.
terms.research_use: Identify government-survival and ministerial-risk events.

terms.plain_language: An organisation representing people with similar political ideas or aims and, when registered, able to have party affiliation shown for endorsed candidates on ballot papers.
terms.research_use: Define canonical party-team entities.

terms.plain_language: A voting system requiring voters to rank candidates in order of preference, with preferences distributed as required to determine the elected candidate.
terms.research_use: Analyse preference flows and final House outcomes.

terms.plain_language: The choice by a political party of its candidate for an election.
terms.research_use: Track candidate-selection changes within parties.

terms.plain_language: The first-preference vote received by a party or candidate before preference distributions.
terms.research_use: Compare first-choice support across elections and polls.

terms.plain_language: An electoral system used in multi-member electorates where representation is broadly proportional to electoral support.
terms.research_use: Interpret Senate election mechanics separately from House contests.

terms.plain_language: A daily parliamentary period in which ministers are asked questions without notice about their responsibilities.
terms.research_use: Track accountability exchanges, claims and ministerial pressure.

terms.plain_language: The redrawing of electoral boundaries so divisions contain approximately equal numbers of electors.
terms.research_use: Control for boundary changes in seat-level historical comparisons.

terms.plain_language: A national vote on a proposed change to the Australian Constitution requiring the constitutional double-majority test.
terms.research_use: Treat constitutional contests separately from ordinary elections.

terms.plain_language: A system in which the government is answerable to Parliament and the ministry must maintain the confidence of the House of Representatives.
terms.research_use: Model government survival and confidence relationships.

terms.plain_language: A member of the main opposition party or parties who acts as spokesperson in an area usually corresponding to a ministerial portfolio.
terms.research_use: Track opposition portfolio responsibility and personnel changes.

terms.plain_language: The number of enrolled electors who voted in an election.
terms.research_use: Analyse participation and denominator effects on vote shares.

terms.plain_language: A count of preferences between the final two candidates in a House of Representatives division.
terms.research_use: Analyse the actual final pair in a seat.

terms.plain_language: An informational House count showing the result as if the final two candidates were from Labor and the Liberal/National Coalition.
terms.research_use: Compare major-side electoral support across time and seats.

terms.plain_language: A document commanding an electoral officer to hold an election and specifying key electoral dates.
terms.research_use: Anchor formal election timetable milestones.
